use_case: Track defect detection (computer vision): a camera kit on the hi-rail truck records the weekly track inspection run, and the vendor's service flags suspected track defects for the inspector's review (registry default 'track and equipment defect detection'; the equipment part is not used)
vendor_or_model: Track defect detection vendor (licensed computer vision model in the vendor's SaaS; SYS-09)
data_categories: Video of track, bridges, grade crossings, and customer sidings, including the propane siding (treated as Restricted); GPS and milepost; flags and the Roadmaster's decisions. Incidental images of people at crossings and on adjacent property
affects_individuals: Yes (indirectly: train crews, roadway workers, and the public depend on safe track; incidental images of people)
human_in_the_loop: The Roadmaster, the designated qualified track inspector under 49 CFR 213.7(b), reviews every flag and still performs every required visual inspection; he alone decides remedial action and slow orders. Model output is ignored on heavily vegetated sections until a retest passes
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 213.233(b) (inspection devices only supplement visual inspection) and 213.7 (C-TRANSPORTATION-S08); 49 CFR part 225 if a missed defect leads to a reportable accident (C-TRANSPORTATION-S05); 49 CFR 1520.9 only if imagery reveals security measures marked SSI (C-TRANSPORTATION-S03); Fla. Stat. 501.171 not triggered (no personal information stored)
status: Pilot since 2026-05-04; approved with conditions 2026-08-31; conditions due 2026-10-31 (contract terms, written human-in-the-loop rule, MFA, data handling)

use_case: Public generative AI chatbots (consumer services) that staff might use to draft letters or summaries

applicable_laws: 49 CFR 1520.9(a) (SSI disclosed only to covered persons with a need to know; C-TRANSPORTATION-S03); POL-02 C.2; POL-04 4.7
